answer: Ephemeral Harbor Keys. Each identity must hold a live session key anchored to a rotating relic of past interaction history; keys expire unless renewed by work a duplicate cannot cheaply fake. Renewal cost scales with how many identities share a network neighborhood (a bounded reef), so clustering sybils raises marginal cost per key. An attacker pays rising renewal fees plus forfeited unused history, roughly O(n²) for n clustered identities.
